setup_code.description: The setup code, which the server writes to its log while setup is pending, as 7K2M-Q9XD-4RTB-H8VW. Case, hyphens, and spaces do not matter, and O is read as 0, and I and L as 1.

signup_policy.description: Who can register an account once setup has completed: closed (no one), invite (people holding an invitation), or open (anyone). Without it, closed. STORYCREEP_SIGNUP overrides it for as long as it is set, as GET /api/v1/setup says.

smtp.description: The SMTP server that the instance sends its email through: the links that verify an email address and reset a password. Without it, the instance sends no email, and an instance admin gives out the links as text. STORYCREEP_SMTP_URL overrides it for as long as it is set, as GET /api/v1/setup says. Setup does not connect to it.

storage.description: The bucket of an S3-compatible object storage that stores the files of the assets, the images that users upload. Without it, the server stores them in its asset directory, /var/lib/storycreep/assets. STORYCREEP_ASSET_STORAGE overrides it for as long as it is set, as GET /api/v1/setup says. Setup does not connect to it.

workspace.description: The first workspace, which the owner owns, and which is the owner's personal workspace. Its default locale is STORYCREEP_DEFAULT_LOCALE.

owner_id.description: The ID of the owner's account, which signs in with POST /api/v1/auth/login

attributes.description: The values that the component holds of its type's attribute definitions that are not in the project's trash, by the definitions' IDs: each a value of its definition's type, as the definition's default is written

component_type_id.description: The ID of the component's type, which is fixed once it is created

deleted_at.description: When the component went to the project's trash, if it is there

description.description: The component's description, a rich-text document (PRD FR-TEXT-01)

image_asset_id.description: The ID of the component's image, an asset of the project, or none

ComponentCreatePayload.description: The payload of a command of the type component.create.

attributes.description: The values that the component holds of its type's attribute definitions that are not in the project's trash, by the definitions' IDs, each a value of its type: true or false for bool; an integer from -9007199254740991 to 9007199254740991 for int, which every runtime holds exactly (PRD §5.8.9), written as 3, 3.0, or 3e0 alike; a number for float, which is read as the nearest double, and is not beyond a double's range; a string of at most 4096 characters for string, and of at most 100000 for text, without control characters but line feeds and tabs; and one of its options for enum. A value of another kind, as a string for an int, is answered with 422 validation_failed, and so is a number written with more than 327 characters, or with an exponent beyond ±999, as a variable's default is. A definition that this leaves out gives the component its default.

description.description: The component's description, a rich-text document (PRD FR-TEXT-01). Without it, an empty paragraph.

folder_id.description: The ID of the folder of components that the component goes into, which is not deleted. Without it, the component goes at the top.

id.description: The new component's ID, a cmp_ ID of a UUIDv7 that the client makes, which no entity of the instance has (PRD §5.2)

image_asset_id.description: The ID of the component's image, an asset of the project. Without it, none.

key.description: The component's key, by which expressions name it, as elara in elara.trust: an identifier of the expression language (PRD §5.8.1): an ASCII letter or an underscore, then ASCII letters, digits, and underscores, of at most 64 characters, as elara, compared case by case, and not one of its reserved words, true, false, and, or, not, global, board, null, if, else, and elseif, which is answered with 422 key_invalid, and that no other component of the project has, of those that are not in its trash, which is answered with 409 key_taken. Without it, the key is derived from the name (PRD FR-COMP-02): its letters and digits in lowercase ASCII, without their accents, each run of other characters an underscore, with an underscore before it if it starts with a digit, or component for a name without them, and with _2, _3, and so on after it if another component of the project that is not in its trash has it, or it is a reserved word.

name.description: The component's name, of 1 to 100 characters, not all of them blank, without white space around it, and without control characters, bidirectional controls, and line separators among them

order.description: The component's place among the children of its folder, or of the top. A key of base-62 digits, 0-9, A-Z, and a-z, that does not end in 0, of at most 128 digits, which orders the children by its bytes, and those with the same key by their IDs without the prefix, cmp_ or fld_, compared by their bytes too: pick one between the keys of the children that it goes between, as V where there are none, 8 between 7 and 9, or 7V between 7 and 8. Without it, the component goes after the last child.

email.description: The email address to invite, which the account that accepts the invitation must have, in any case. Without it, the invitation is a link invitation, which whoever holds its link may accept, with any account.

role.description: The role that accepting the invitation gives. Only an owner invites someone as owner, and an admin is answered with 403 owner_required.

name.description: The project's name, of 1 to 100 characters, not all of them blank, and without control characters, bidirectional controls, and line separators among them. White space around it is removed.

expires_at.description: When the token expires, in RFC 3339, which must be in the future, and which the server keeps to the microsecond, as the answer gives it; without it, the token does not expire

name.description: The token's name, which says what it is for, of 1 to 100 characters, not all of them blank, and without control characters, bidirectional controls, and line separators among them. White space around it is removed.

scopes.description: The scopes that the token holds, one at least, each kept once: snapshot:read reads the published snapshots; project:read reads the draft too, and implies snapshot:read; project:write changes the draft, and implies project:read; snapshot:write publishes snapshots, and implies snapshot:read; and export:read is the authoring-data export, which no other scope implies. A token that must not see unreleased work, such as a CI job's that only pulls releases, holds snapshot:read alone.

default_locale.description: The workspace's default locale, as a BCP 47 tag of a locale that the server has a catalog for. Without it, the locale of the request: the one that its Accept-Language prefers among those, or else STORYCREEP_DEFAULT_LOCALE.

name.description: The workspace's name, of 1 to 100 characters, not all of them blank, and without control characters, bidirectional controls and line separators among them. White space around it is removed.

slug.description: The workspace's slug: groups of lowercase ASCII letters and digits joined by single hyphens, of at most 64 characters, and not a reserved word, or the answer is 422 slug_invalid; if another workspace has it, the answer is 409 slug_taken. Without it, the slug is derived from the name: its letters and digits in lowercase ASCII, without accents, each run of other characters a hyphen, cut to 64 characters, or workspace if the name has none. If another workspace has that slug, or it is a reserved word, -2, -3, and so on up to -10 is added, and after that a random suffix of 8 lowercase letters and digits.

expires_at.description: When the token expires, after which every request made with it is answered with 401 unauthenticated; a token without it does not expire

last_used_at.description: When a request was last made with the token, to the minute; a token without it has not been used

name.description: The token's name

project_id.description: The ID of the project that the token is narrowed to, on which alone it acts; a token without it acts on every project of its workspace

scopes.description: The scopes that the token holds: snapshot:read reads the published snapshots; project:read reads the draft too, and implies snapshot:read; project:write changes the draft, and implies project:read; snapshot:write publishes snapshots, and implies snapshot:read; and export:read is the authoring-data export, which no other scope implies

secret.description: The token's secret, which starts with scp_, and which a request sends as Authorization: Bearer <secret>. This is the only answer that holds it: the server keeps only its SHA-256 hash, so keep it now, as a secret.

user_id.description: The ID of the account that made the token and owns it: a request made with the token does no more than the owner's role allows at the time

workspace_id.description: The ID of the workspace that the token belongs to, and acts in alone

code.description: A stable error code; docs/error-codes.md lists them

details.description: More about the error, for programs; the code decides the keys

message.description: What went wrong, for people, in the language that the Content-Language header names

display_name.description: The name that other people see, of 1 to 100 characters, not all of them blank, and without control characters, bidirectional controls and line separators among them. White space around it is removed.

email.description: The account's email address, which signs in: an address alone, as jo@example.com, of at most 254 bytes, without spaces or characters that are not printed. Addresses compare without regard to case or to how their characters are composed.

password.description: The password: at least 12 characters, and not one of the most common passwords, or the answer is weak_password.

display_name.description: The name that other people see, as for POST /api/v1/auth/register

email.description: The account's email address, as for POST /api/v1/auth/register. An invitation to an address takes only that address, as citext compares them, and the address is the invitation's when this is left out; a link invitation needs one.

token.description: The token of the invitation's link: what follows token= in the fragment of the URL that the link opens

new_password.description: The new password: at least 12 characters, and not one of the most common passwords, or the answer is weak_password

token.description: The token of the link that resets the password: what follows token= in the fragment of the URL that the link opens

RichTextAttributeId.description: A component type's attribute definition's ID.

RichTextDecimals.description: The number of digits after the point that a number is shown with, rounded half away from zero. A value that is not a number is shown as it is.

RichTextDoc.description: A document: its blocks, at least one. The editor's empty document is one empty paragraph.

RichTextHardBreak.description: A line break within a paragraph.

RichTextLink.description: A link to an absolute http or https URL with a host, without white space, or a mailto URL of one address and nothing else.

RichTextList.description: A list, bulleted (bulletList) or numbered (orderedList), of at least one item. Lists nest at most 5 deep, which the server checks beyond this schema.

attrs.description: An orderedList's attributes. A bulletList has none, which the server checks beyond this schema.

start.description: The number of the first item, 1 when it is not given.

RichTextListItem.description: A list item: a paragraph, then any paragraphs and lists. That it starts with a paragraph is checked by the server, beyond this schema.

RichTextMarks.description: The marks of an inline node, each at most once, which the server checks beyond this schema. The code mark is not combined with another.

RichTextMention.description: A mention of a component, which the text shows by the component's name.

RichTextParagraph.description: A paragraph, which may be empty.

RichTextText.description: Text, without control characters but tabs, or line and paragraph separators: a line break is a hardBreak, and a paragraph a paragraph. Nor does it hold bidirectional controls, as U+202E, which the server checks beyond this schema. A document's texts hold at most 100,000 characters together.

RichTextValueRef.description: A reference to a value, which the text shows as the runtime renders it: a variable's, or a runtime attribute's of a component.

current.description: Whether it is the session of the request

expires_at.description: When it ends at the latest, however often it is used: STORYCREEP_SESSION_LIFETIME after its user signed in, or the lifetime in force when its user signed in, if that was shorter

idle_expires_at.description: When it ends unless it is used before: STORYCREEP_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT after its last use, or at expires_at if that is sooner

ip.description: The IP address that its user signed in from: the address that the connection came from, or, if that is one of STORYCREEP_TRUSTED_PROXIES, the client's address that the proxies forwarded

last_seen_at.description: When it was last used, to the minute

user_agent.description: The User-Agent header of the client that its user signed in with

role.description: The member's role on the project: admin, editor, commenter, or viewer. owner is a role of the workspace alone, and is answered with 400 owner_not_grantable.

signup_policy.description: The signup policy that the configuration sets, if it sets one, or else the one that setup records when the request names none: closed.

signup_policy_fixed.description: Whether the configuration sets the signup policy, with STORYCREEP_SIGNUP, or because the instance is hosted, which then overrides the policy that setup records, for as long as it sets it. A setup screen offers no choice of policy then.

smtp_fixed.description: Whether the configuration sets the SMTP server, with STORYCREEP_SMTP_URL, which then overrides the one that setup records, for as long as it sets it. A setup screen asks for no SMTP server then.

storage_fixed.description: Whether the configuration sets where the files of the assets are stored, with STORYCREEP_ASSET_STORAGE, which then overrides the bucket that setup records, for as long as it sets it. A setup screen asks for no bucket then.

display_name.description: The owner's display name, as for POST /api/v1/auth/register

email.description: The owner's email address, which signs in, as for POST /api/v1/auth/register

password.description: The owner's password: at least 12 characters, and not one of the most common passwords, or the answer is weak_password.

from.description: The address that the instance's email comes from, alone or with a name, as Storycreep <noreply@example.com>, which the server must let it send from

host.description: The SMTP server's host name or IP address

password.description: The password that signs in to the server, with the username

port.description: The SMTP server's port, as 587 for starttls or 465 for tls

security.description: How the connection is protected: tls, from its start; starttls, which the server must offer, before anything is sent; or none, for a relay on the same host or network, which then cannot sign in unless it is on localhost, 127.0.0.1, or ::1

username.description: The username that signs in to the server, with PLAIN or LOGIN, with the password; without it, the server is not signed in to

access_key_id.description: The access key ID of the keys that read, write, list, and delete the bucket's objects

bucket.description: The bucket, which must exist: 3 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, dots, and hyphens

host.description: The host name or IP address of the S3-compatible object storage, as s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com, which the users' browsers must reach too, because they read the files through URLs of it that the server signs

port.description: The storage's port; without it, 443 for tls and 80 for none

region.description: The bucket's region, as eu-central-1; without it, us-east-1, which MinIO and most S3-compatible storages take

secret_access_key.description: The secret key of those keys

security.description: How the connection is protected: tls, HTTPS, which is the default, or none, plain HTTP, which the users' browsers read the files over too, for an instance that is itself served over plain HTTP, as on a local network

name.description: The workspace's name, as for POST /api/v1/workspaces

slug.description: The workspace's slug, as for POST /api/v1/workspaces, with the same errors. Without it, the slug is derived from the name.

csrf_token.description: The session's CSRF token: every request made with the session that changes something, with a method other than GET, HEAD, or OPTIONS, sends it in its X-CSRF-Token header, or is answered with 403 csrf_failed. It stays the same for as long as the session does, until changing the password gives the session a new one.

user_id.description: The ID of the account that is signed in

component_type_id.description: The ID of the component's type, which is fixed once it is created

deleted_at.description: When the component went to the project's trash, if it is there

folder_id.description: The ID of the folder of components that the component is in, if it is in one, or none for a component at the top

image_asset_id.description: The ID of the component's image, an asset of the project, or none

key.description: The component's key, by which expressions name it, as elara in elara.trust: an identifier of the expression language (PRD §5.8.1), unique among the project's components that are not in its trash. A change of the component's name leaves it as it is (PRD FR-COMP-02 AC2).

name.description: The component's name, as Elara

order.description: The component's place among the folders and components of its folder, or of the top: they are ordered by their order, compared by its bytes, then by their IDs without the prefix, cmp_ or fld_, compared by their bytes too (package orderkey)

project_id.description: The ID of the component's project

rev.description: The component's revision, which every change of it increments, a change of one of its values or of the attribute definitions whose values it holds among them, and which a change expects with expected_rev

deleted_at.description: When the entity was deleted to the trash

kind.description: What the entity is: a board, a variable, or a component, and, once they exist, a node (PRD FR-PROJ-06). The command of its kind, as board.restore, restores it with its ID as id.

name.description: The entity's name, or a variable's key

purge_after.description: When the entity's time in the trash ends. The purge, which runs every hour, deletes it for good then; until it does, the entity can be restored.

deleted_at.description: When the component went to the project's trash, if it is there: a retype converts the values of the components in the trash too

name.description: The component's name

default_locale.description: The new locale of the project's text, as a BCP 47 tag of a language

description.description: The project's new description, as for POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/projects; empty for none

entry.description: The project's new entry, which replaces its entry: an object without board_id removes it. node_id needs board_id. A board other than the entry's is one of the project's boards, in its trash or not, or the answer is 422 validation_failed; the node needs not exist yet.

expected_rev.description: The project's revision that the change was made against. If the project has another, the answer is 409 revision_conflict, and nothing changes. Without it, the change is made whatever the revision. A body that names no field to change changes nothing, so it is answered with the project, whatever its revision.

name.description: The project's new name, as for POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/projects. The project keeps its slug.

publish_min_role.description: The least role that may publish the project's snapshots: editor, or admin to keep editors from publishing (PRD FR-SNAP-01 AC3). A change is recorded in the audit log.

slug.description: The project's new slug, which the published format's manifest shows: groups of lowercase ASCII letters and digits joined by single hyphens, as harbour, of at most 64 characters, that is not a name that Windows reserves for a device, such as con or com1. A slug that is not one is answered with 422 slug_invalid.

default_locale.description: The workspace's new default locale, a BCP 47 tag of a locale that the server has a catalog for

name.description: The workspace's new name, as for POST /api/v1/workspaces

slug.description: The workspace's new slug, as for POST /api/v1/workspaces, with the same errors. A slug that the workspace has already is kept, as a reserved word that a later release added to the list is.

api_requests.description: The requests that the workspace's API tokens have made: each that a token was accepted for, whatever its answer then; a request that a token is refused for, as one without the route's scope, is not counted

boards.description: The boards of the workspace's projects that are in no trash: neither in their project's nor, with their project, in the workspace's

nodes.description: The nodes of the workspace's projects

projects.description: The workspace's projects that count towards its limit: those that are neither archived nor in its trash

snapshots.description: The snapshots of the workspace's projects

storage_bytes.description: The bytes that the workspace's stored files take up. Uploads that run at once may take it past its limit by what they add together.

board_id.description: The ID of the variable's board, for a variable of a board, or none for a global

default.description: The variable's default, a value of its type: true or false for bool, an integer for int, a number for float, which is written without a decimal point when it is integral, as 2, and a string for string. A client reads a number by the variable's type, never by how it is written (PRD §5.8.9).

deleted_at.description: When the variable went to the project's trash, if it is there: when it was deleted, or, if it was not, but its board is in the trash, with which it is in the trash too, and comes back, when the board was deleted

description.description: The variable's description, which may be empty

folder_id.description: The ID of the folder of variables that the variable is in, if it is in one, or none for a variable at the top

key.description: The variable's key, by which expressions name it: an identifier of the expression language (PRD §5.8.1), unique among the project's global variables, or among its board's, that are not in the trash

order.description: The variable's place among the folders and variables of its folder, or of the top: they are ordered by their order, compared by its bytes, then by their IDs without the prefix, var_ or fld_, compared by their bytes too (package orderkey)

project_id.description: The ID of the variable's project

reset_on_enter.description: Whether the variable is reset to its default each time the flow enters its board (PRD FR-VAR-02), which only a board's variable may be

rev.description: The variable's revision, which every change of it increments, and which a change expects with expected_rev

scope.description: Who reads the variable: every board's expressions, for global, or only its board's, for board (PRD FR-VAR-02). A board's variable keeps its value across the board's entries, as a global does, unless reset_on_enter is set.

command_id.description: The command's ID, a UUID that the client makes, unique within the project. A command whose ID the project's batches applied already is answered as it was, and not applied again.

board_id.description: The ID of the variable's board, which is not in the project's trash, if scope is board. A global variable has none.

default.description: The variable's default, a value of its type: true or false for bool; an integer from -9007199254740991 to 9007199254740991 for int, which every runtime holds exactly (PRD §5.8.9), written as 3, 3.0, or 3e0 alike; a number for float, which is read as the nearest double, and is not beyond a double's range; and a string of at most 4096 characters, without control characters but line feeds and tabs, for string. A value of another kind, as a string for an int (PRD FR-VAR-01 AC2), is answered with 422 validation_failed. A number written with more than 327 characters, or with an exponent beyond ±999, as 0e1000, is answered with 422 validation_failed, whatever it reads as: no int or float needs more, the longest, -5e-324 written without an exponent, as the server may write a number back, having 327. A number beyond a double's range, as 1e400 or 1e1000, is answered with 400 invalid_request as the API reads the body, unless it is written with more than 327 characters, which the API's reader may take for a number within the range, and which is then answered with 422 validation_failed. Without it, the type's zero value: false, 0, 0.0, or the empty string.

description.description: The variable's description, of at most 2000 characters, without white space around it, and without control characters but line feeds and tabs. Without it, the variable has none.

folder_id.description: The ID of the folder of variables that the variable goes into, which is not deleted. Without it, the variable goes at the top.

id.description: The new variable's ID, a var_ ID of a UUIDv7 that the client makes, which no entity of the instance has (PRD §5.2)

key.description: The variable's key, by which expressions name it: an identifier of the expression language (PRD §5.8.1): an ASCII letter or an underscore, then ASCII letters, digits, and underscores, of at most 64 characters, as met_elara, compared case by case, and not one of its reserved words, true, false, and, or, not, global, board, null, if, else, and elseif, which is answered with 422 key_invalid, and that no other variable of its scope has, of those that are not in the project's trash, the project's global variables for a global, and its board's for a board's, which is answered with 409 key_taken.

order.description: The variable's place among the children of its folder, or of the top. A key of base-62 digits, 0-9, A-Z, and a-z, that does not end in 0, of at most 128 digits, which orders the children by its bytes, and those with the same key by their IDs without the prefix, var_ or fld_, compared by their bytes too: pick one between the keys of the children that it goes between, as V where there are none, 8 between 7 and 9, or 7V between 7 and 8. Without it, the variable goes after the last child.

reset_on_enter.description: Whether the variable is reset to its default each time the flow enters its board (PRD FR-VAR-02, §5.8.5), which only a board's variable may be. Without it, false.

scope.description: Who reads the variable: every board's expressions, for global, or only its board's, for board (PRD FR-VAR-02). A board's variable keeps its value across the board's entries, as a global does, unless reset_on_enter is set.

post.description: Returns a link that resets the password of the active account that the email address belongs to, which lasts an hour, and is used once with POST /api/v1/auth/password-reset/confirm. It is for an instance that sends no email, whose links an instance admin gives out instead, to the account's user alone, because whoever holds a link can use it; an instance that sends email answers 403 email_configured. A user who is not an instance admin, such as a workspace's owner or admin, is answered with 403 instance_admin_required, whatever the request holds. An address that belongs to no active account is answered with 404 not_found. The audit log records the issue. It needs a signed-in user: the session cookie that POST /api/v1/auth/login sets, or the answer is 401 unauthenticated. It is session-only: a request made with an API token, whatever its scopes, is answered with 403 session_required (PRD FR-AUTH-04). It changes something, so it also needs the session's CSRF token in the X-CSRF-Token header, or the answer is 403 csrf_failed. Signing in, registering, changing a password, completing first-run setup, asking for a link that resets a password or verifies an email address, using one, an instance admin's taking one as text, inviting someone to a workspace, sending an invitation anew, reading, accepting, or registering with an invitation's link, and making, listing, or revoking an API token share a rate limit of 20 requests a minute for each IP address. Registering, with an invitation or without, and asking for a link that resets a password also share one of 10 a minute for each email address, so that each counts against the other for the same address, and changing a password, asking for a link that verifies the signed-in account's email address, an instance admin's taking a link as text, inviting someone, sending an invitation anew, accepting one, and making, listing, or revoking an API token share one of 10 a minute for each account. No request made with an API token counts against these, so that the requests of a token, which count against its owner's account too, cannot keep the owner from finding and revoking it, after which no limit counts them. The RateLimit headers say how much of the limit of the IP address, or of the account, is left, and a request over a limit is answered with 429 rate_limited, whose details.reason is rate, whose RateLimit headers report the limit that it is over, that of the email address included, and whose Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait.

post.summary: Ask for a link that verifies the account's email address

post.description: Signs in with an account's email address and password, and starts a session, whose secret the Set-Cookie header gives the client, and whose CSRF token the body holds. The account's first sign-in also gives it its personal workspace, named after its display name, which it owns; GET /api/v1/workspaces lists it. Where the instance always sends email, as hosted mode does, that is the first sign-in once the account's email address is verified, or the verification itself. An address of no account, a wrong password, and an account that cannot sign in, such as a suspended one, are all answered with 401 invalid_credentials, after the same work, so that the answer does not tell them apart. A request that a browser's Sec-Fetch-Site header says comes from another site, or from another origin of the same site, is answered with 403 csrf_failed; browsers send that header only to https URLs and to loopback addresses, such as localhost. After 10 failed sign-ins in a row with an email address, whether or not it belongs to an account, the address is locked for a minute, and each further failure, once a lock ends, locks it for twice as long as the lock before, up to 15 minutes: while it is locked, every sign-in with it is answered with 429 rate_limited, whose details.reason is locked, even with the right password. A successful sign-in forgets the failures, and so do 24 hours without one. Signing in, registering, changing a password, completing first-run setup, asking for a link that resets a password or verifies an email address, using one, an instance admin's taking one as text, inviting someone to a workspace, sending an invitation anew, reading, accepting, or registering with an invitation's link, and making, listing, or revoking an API token share a rate limit of 20 requests a minute for each IP address. delete.description: Revokes one of the signed-in account's active sessions, which is then no longer valid on any server. Revoking the session of the request signs it out, and the answer clears its cookie. A session that is not an active session of the account is answered with 404 not_found. It changes something, so it also needs the session's CSRF token in the X-CSRF-Token header, or the answer is 403 csrf_failed. Requests that change something share a rate limit of 600 a minute for each IP address, and 300 for each account. post.description: Records that the email address of the account of a link that verifies it is verified, and uses the link, which works once, and only while the address is still the account's. Where the instance requires a verified address before a workspace can be created, as hosted mode does, it also gives the account its personal workspace, if it has had none; should that fail, the answer is still 204, because the address is verified, and the account's next sign-in gives the workspace. Registering, with an invitation or without, and asking for a link that resets a password also share one of 10 a minute for each email address, so that each counts against the other for the same address, and changing a password, asking for a link that verifies the signed-in account's email address, an instance admin's taking a link as text, inviting someone, sending an invitation anew, accepting one, and making, listing, or revoking an API token share one of 10 a minute for each account. No request made with an API token counts against these, so that the requests of a token, which count against its owner's account too, cannot keep the owner from finding and revoking it, after which no limit counts them. post.description: Creates an account, as POST /api/v1/auth/register does, and accepts an invitation with its link as the new account, which joins the invitation's workspace with its role, under the invite and the open signup policies. Until first-run setup has completed, the answer is 403 setup_required, whatever the policy. Under closed, the answer is 403 signup_closed, whatever the request holds, and only an account that exists already accepts an invitation, with POST /api/v1/invites/accept. An invitation to an address registers that address, and another is answered with 403 invite_email_mismatch (FR-TEN-02 AC3). A token that belongs to no invitation, as one that sending the invitation anew replaced, or whose workspace no longer exists, is answered with 400 token_invalid, an invitation that has been revoked with 410 invite_revoked, one that has been accepted with 410 invite_accepted, and one that has expired with 410 invite_expired (FR-TEN-02 AC1). A link invitation, which registers any address, to a workspace that has as many members as it may have, as POST /api/v1/invites/accept says, is answered with 409 limit_exceeded, whatever the address, for as long as the workspace is full, so that its link, which stays open, does not register one account after another. The fields are checked as POST /api/v1/auth/register checks them, with its errors. Otherwise the answer is 202 without a body, whether or not the address has an account already, so that it does not tell whether an address has one: an account that exists stays as it was, and the invitation stays open for it. So it does for a new account, which joins no workspace, if the workspace of an invitation to an address is full. The client then signs in, and accepts the invitation with POST /api/v1/invites/accept, which returns the membership either way, or answers 409 limit_exceeded while the workspace is full. post.description:
Applies a batch of commands to a project, every change of whose content is a command of a type that the body's schema describes, with its payload (PRD FR-API-03). The body is a batch, {"commands": [...]}, or a list of batches, {"batches": [{"commands": [...]}, ...]}. A batch applies whole, in one transaction, or not at all, and is one step of undo. Each command is authorised by the signed-in user's role as its type's operation of the permission matrix needs (PRD §5.6), and a role that does not allow one refuses its batch with 403 insufficient_role, or owner_required. A batch with a command that only a session may apply, as deleting or restoring the project, which an API token sends is refused with 403 session_required, whatever the token's scopes (PRD FR-AUTH-04). A project that does not exist, is in the trash, or on which the signed-in user's role is none, as it is for a user who is not a member of its workspace or a guest without a grant on it, is answered with 404 not_found, so that the answer does not tell whether it exists. So is a project that the request's API token does not cover: one of another workspace, or one other than the project that the token is narrowed to (PRD FR-AUTH-04 AC3). Every expected_rev of a batch is checked against the entities as they are before the batch, and a stale one refuses it with 409 revision_conflict, whose details hold the entities' current revisions and states. An archived project refuses a batch with 409 project_archived, unless each of its commands applies to an archived project, and a batch that would take the workspace past a limit of its plan is refused with 409 limit_exceeded. A batch that its schema, or its commands' own checks, refuse is answered with 422 validation_failed, whose details locate each problem, as body.commands[2].payload.name. A command may also refuse its batch for what the project's state makes of its payload, at the payload's field, as body.commands[0].payload.folder_id: with 422 validation_failed for a value that the state does not take, as the ID of a folder that the project does not have, or that is deleted, or with the code that the field's description names, as 422 slug_invalid for a slug that is not one, 409 slug_taken for a slug that another board has, 409 folder_not_empty for a folder to delete that holds folders, boards, variables, or components, 422 key_invalid for a key of a variable, a component type, an attribute definition, or a component that is not an identifier, 409 key_taken for a key that another entity of its scope has, or 409 component_type_in_use for a component type to delete of which a component that is not in the trash is. A batch whose undo, the inverses of its commands as the operation log keeps them, would take more than 4 MiB, so that the batch that undoes it would not fit in a request, is refused with 422 validation_failed at the command that takes it past: at its payload, as body.commands[3].payload, or at the field whose change the undo holds the values of, as body.commands[3].payload.type for an attribute.retype that would lose too much. The batch that undoes another is bounded alike, by its own undo, which writes again what the other's commands wrote, so the undo of a batch whose commands wrote more than 4 MiB, as several large descriptions over small ones, is refused so too, and is sent in smaller batches.

A command_id is the client's, unique within the project, and makes the batch idempotent. A batch sent again, as when its answer was lost, is answered as it was the first time and applies nothing again, before the project's state and the workspace's limits are checked: the same batch, with the same commands in the same order, for at least 24 hours, whether it applied or was refused with revision_conflict, project_archived, or limit_exceeded; after that, a batch whose commands applied is answered with the status already_applied, the seq that applied them, and the current revisions of the entities that they changed, and one that was refused is checked anew. So is any other batch whose commands were all applied before, however they are grouped. A batch with commands that were applied and commands that were not is refused with 422 idempotency_mismatch, which lists the applied ones, and applies nothing. A command's payload is not compared with the one that its ID was applied with. Any other refusal, as of the role, is checked anew when the batch is sent again.

A request of a list of batches applies each, in its own transaction, in the order of the list, and is answered with 200 and a result of each, applied or rejected with its error, so that a rejected batch, of any of the refusals above, never keeps the later ones from applying. A body that is neither form, or has more than 100 batches, is answered with 422 validation_failed, and a batch of more than 1000 commands is rejected so. A body that is not one strict JSON value, as one with a key twice in an object, anywhere in it, is answered with 400 invalid_request, as on every route. The body is at most 5 MB, as every route's, and a larger one is answered with 413 request_too_large, so that a request of many large batches may need to be split. It needs a signed-in user: the session cookie that POST /api/v1/auth/login sets, or an API token that holds the scope project:write, or a scope that implies it, as Authorization: Bearer <token>; otherwise the answer is 401 unauthenticated, or 403 insufficient_scope for a token without the scope, each with the Bearer scheme's challenge in its WWW-Authenticate header (RFC 6750). A request made with a token does no more than the token's owner's role allows at the time. It changes something, so a request made with the session cookie also needs the session's CSRF token in the X-CSRF-Token header, or the answer is 403 csrf_failed; a request made with a token needs none. Requests that change something share a rate limit of 600 a minute for each IP address, 300 for each account, and 300 for each API token, whose requests count against its owner's account too. The RateLimit headers say how much is left of the limit of whichever of them has the fewest requests left, and a request over a limit is answered with 429 rate_limited, whose details.bucket is write, and whose Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait.

get.description: Lists what is in the project's trash, the most recently deleted first: its boards, variables, and components, and, once they exist, its nodes, each with its kind. Each stays in the trash for 30 days from its deletion, until its purge_after, when a purge that runs every hour deletes it for good; until then, the command of its kind restores it where it was, as board.restore with its ID, through POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/commands. A board's variables are in the trash with it, unlisted, come back with it, and are purged with it, a variable of the board deleted on its own among them, which is listed, and restored only once its board is. A deleted folder is not listed: restoring a board restores the deleted folders above it, and the purge deletes a deleted folder once its 30 days have passed and it holds nothing. Neither is a deleted component type or attribute definition: a type's definitions are in the trash with it, restoring a component restores its type, and the purge deletes a type once its 30 days have passed and it holds no component. Nothing in the trash is in the project's other reads. A project that does not exist, is in the trash, or on which the signed-in user's role is none, as it is for a user who is not a member of its workspace or a guest without a grant on it, is answered with 404 not_found, so that the answer does not tell whether it exists. A request made with a token does no more than the token's owner's role allows at the time. Requests that read share a rate limit of 1,200 a minute for each IP address, 600 for each account, and 600 for each API token, whose requests count against its owner's account too. get.description: Returns a variable of the project. They change through the project's command endpoint, POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/commands, whose commands of the type variable.* create, rename, describe, retype, rescope, move, delete, and restore them, and change their defaults and reset_on_enter. A project that does not exist, is in the trash, or on which the signed-in user's role is none, as it is for a user who is not a member of its workspace or a guest without a grant on it, is answered with 404 not_found, so that the answer does not tell whether it exists. So is a project that the request's API token does not cover: one of another workspace, or one other than the project that the token is narrowed to (PRD FR-AUTH-04 AC3). A variable that the project does not have, or that is in its trash, as one of a board in the trash is, is answered with 404 not_found. It needs a signed-in user: the session cookie that POST /api/v1/auth/login sets, or an API token that holds the scope project:read, or a scope that implies it, as Authorization: Bearer <token>; otherwise the answer is 401 unauthenticated, or 403 insufficient_scope for a token without the scope, each with the Bearer scheme's challenge in its WWW-Authenticate header (RFC 6750). A request made with a token does no more than the token's owner's role allows at the time. Requests that read share a rate limit of 1,200 a minute for each IP address, 600 for each account, and 600 for each API token, whose requests count against its owner's account too. The RateLimit headers say how much is left of the limit of whichever of them has the fewest requests left, and a request over a limit is answered with 429 rate_limited, whose details.bucket is read, and whose Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait.

post.description: Completes the instance's first-run setup, once: creates the first owner's account, which is an instance admin, and the first workspace, which the owner owns, and records the signup policy, the SMTP server, and the bucket of the assets' files. Until then, POST /api/v1/auth/register answers 403 setup_required, whatever the policy. The setup code, which the server writes to its log while setup is pending, must be the instance's, or the answer is 403 invalid_setup_code. A field that the request does not allow, as an SMTP server's host that is not one, a username without a password, a bucket's name in capitals, or an email address that has an account, as one that storycreep create-user made, is answered with 422 validation_failed. Of two setups at once, one completes, and the other is answered with 404 not_found. The owner then signs in with POST /api/v1/auth/login. Once setup has completed, the answer is 404 not_found, for everyone, and stays so. Signing in, registering, changing a password, completing first-run setup, asking for a link that resets a password or verifies an email address, using one, an instance admin's taking one as text, inviting someone to a workspace, sending an invitation anew, reading, accepting, or registering with an invitation's link, and making, listing, or revoking an API token share a rate limit of 20 requests a minute for each IP address. Registering, with an invitation or without, and asking for a link that resets a password also share one of 10 a minute for each email address, so that each counts against the other for the same address, and changing a password, asking for a link that verifies the signed-in account's email address, an instance admin's taking a link as text, inviting someone, sending an invitation anew, accepting one, and making, listing, or revoking an API token share one of 10 a minute for each account. No request made with an API token counts against these, so that the requests of a token, which count against its owner's account too, cannot keep the owner from finding and revoking it, after which no limit counts them. The RateLimit headers say how much of the limit of the IP address, or of the account, is left, and a request over a limit is answered with 429 rate_limited, whose details.reason is rate, whose RateLimit headers report the limit that it is over, that of the email address included, and whose Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait.

get.description: Lists the workspaces that the signed-in user is a member of, in the order of their IDs, oldest first, each with the role of the user's membership, guest included. A client switches between them by naming one by its ID in the routes that it calls: the server keeps no current workspace. The RateLimit headers say how much is left of the limit of whichever of them has the fewest requests left, and a request over a limit is answered with 429 rate_limited, whose details.bucket is read, and whose Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait.

post.description: Creates a workspace, whose owner the signed-in user becomes. Where the instance always sends email, as hosted mode does, a user who has not verified their email address is answered with 403 email_unverified, whatever the request holds. A name or a default locale that its field does not allow is answered with 422 validation_failed. It needs a signed-in user: the session cookie that POST /api/v1/auth/login sets, or the answer is 401 unauthenticated. It is session-only: a request made with an API token, whatever its scopes, is answered with 403 session_required (PRD FR-AUTH-04). It changes something, so it also needs the session's CSRF token in the X-CSRF-Token header, or the answer is 403 csrf_failed. Requests that change something share a rate limit of 600 a minute for each IP address, and 300 for each account. The RateLimit headers say how much is left of the limit of whichever of the two has the fewest requests left, and a request over a limit is answered with 429 rate_limited, whose details.bucket is write, and whose Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait.

post.description: Invites an email address, or, without one, whoever holds the invitation's link, to join a workspace with a role, for 14 days. Only an owner invites someone as owner, and an admin is answered with 403 owner_required. Only an owner or an admin of the workspace may, and anyone else with a role in it is answered with 403 insufficient_role. A workspace that does not exist, or in which the signed-in user's role is none, as it is for a user who is not a member or is a guest, is answered with 404 not_found, so that the answer does not tell whether it exists. An address that belongs to a member of the workspace is answered with 409 already_member, and one that has an open invitation of the workspace already, expired or not, with 409 invite_exists. On an instance that sends email, as GET /api/v1/instance says, an invitation to an address is emailed, with a link that lasts its 14 days from when the email is sent, and the answer holds no link. A workspace that does not exist, or of which the signed-in user is neither a member nor an instance admin who acts as its owner, as with STORYCREEP_INSTANCE_ADMIN_ACCESS on, is answered with 404 not_found, so that the answer does not tell whether it exists. So is a workspace other than the one that the request's API token belongs to, and a token narrowed to a project is shown that project alone (PRD FR-AUTH-04 AC3). It needs a signed-in user: the session cookie that POST /api/v1/auth/login sets, or an API token that holds the scope snapshot:read, or a scope that implies it, as Authorization: Bearer <token>; otherwise the answer is 401 unauthenticated, or 403 insufficient_scope for a token without the scope, each with the Bearer scheme's challenge in its WWW-Authenticate header (RFC 6750). A request made with a token does no more than the token's owner's role allows at the time. Requests that read share a rate limit of 1,200 a minute for each IP address, 600 for each account, and 600 for each API token, whose requests count against its owner's account too. The RateLimit headers say how much is left of the limit of whichever of them has the fewest requests left, and a request over a limit is answered with 429 rate_limited, whose details.bucket is read, and whose Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait.

A workspace that does not exist, or in which the signed-in user's role is none, as it is for a user who is not a member or is a guest, is answered with 404 not_found, so that the answer does not tell whether it exists. It is session-only: a request made with an API token, whatever its scopes, is answered with 403 session_required (PRD FR-AUTH-04). It changes something, so it also needs the session's CSRF token in the X-CSRF-Token header, or the answer is 403 csrf_failed. Requests that change something share a rate limit of 600 a minute for each IP address, and 300 for each account. The RateLimit headers say how much is left of the limit of whichever of the two has the fewest requests left, and a request over a limit is answered with 429 rate_limited, whose details.bucket is write, and whose Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait.

get.description: Lists the API tokens of the whole workspace that are not revoked, expired ones included, in the order of their IDs, oldest first, without their secrets: every member's, to an owner or an admin of the workspace, and their own, to an editor. Anyone else with a role in it is answered with 403 insufficient_role. The tokens narrowed to a project are listed by GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/tokens. A workspace that does not exist, or in which the signed-in user's role is none, as it is for a user who is not a member or is a guest, is answered with 404 not_found, so that the answer does not tell whether it exists. It needs a signed-in user: the session cookie that POST /api/v1/auth/login sets, or the answer is 401 unauthenticated. It is session-only: a request made with an API token, whatever its scopes, is answered with 403 session_required (PRD FR-AUTH-04). It refuses every API token so that no token makes, lists, or revokes another. Signing in, registering, changing a password, completing first-run setup, asking for a link that resets a password or verifies an email address, using one, an instance admin's taking one as text, inviting someone to a workspace, sending an invitation anew, reading, accepting, or registering with an invitation's link, and making, listing, or revoking an API token share a rate limit of 20 requests a minute for each IP address. Registering, with an invitation or without, and asking for a link that resets a password also share one of 10 a minute for each email address, so that each counts against the other for the same address, and changing a password, asking for a link that verifies the signed-in account's email address, an instance admin's taking a link as text, inviting someone, sending an invitation anew, accepting one, and making, listing, or revoking an API token share one of 10 a minute for each account. No request made with an API token counts against these, so that the requests of a token, which count against its owner's account too, cannot keep the owner from finding and revoking it, after which no limit counts them. The RateLimit headers say how much of the limit of the IP address, or of the account, is left, and a request over a limit is answered with 429 rate_limited, whose details.reason is rate, whose RateLimit headers report the limit that it is over, that of the email address included, and whose Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait.

On an operation that a rate limit counts, as every operation of the API is, how many requests of its kind the client may make in a window of time, for its IP address, its account, or the API token that it makes the request with, whichever has the fewest left, or, with 429 rate_limited whose details.reason is rate, for the one that used up its limit, which may be the email address that the request names. With details.reason locked, no limit is used up: the email address is locked, and the headers report the IP address or the account as on any other answer. An answer to a request refused before the rate limit counts it has none of the RateLimit headers: one without valid credentials, a CSRF token, or an API token's scope where the operation needs them, one that the signup policy or another check of the operation refuses before it counts, one made while the server is not ready, and one whose count failed, with internal_error
On an operation that a rate limit counts, how many more requests of its kind the client may make in the current window, for the same key as RateLimit-Limit
On an operation that a rate limit counts, how many seconds until the current window ends, and the limit is whole again
How many seconds to wait before trying again, with 429 rate_limited and 503 not_ready

The challenge of the Bearer scheme (RFC 6750 §3): with 401 unauthenticated from a route that takes an API token, and to a request whose API token is not valid, with error="invalid_token", and with 403 insufficient_scope, with error="insufficient_scope" and the scope that the route needs
